title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy setting for profanity filtering in transcripts
summary: The briefing accurately reports the default, organiser-policy scope, rollout and documented PowerShell control, including the reference page's release caveat. Two minor table omissions remain: meeting-policy assignment and the separately discussed absence of a tenant-wide master switch.

claims.claim: The new Teams meeting policy controls profanity masking in live transcription.
claims.quote: Teams administrators will be able to use a meeting policy to control whether profane words are masked in live transcription and saved meeting transcripts.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0]; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The same control governs profanity masking in saved meeting transcripts.
claims.quote: Teams administrators will be able to use a meeting policy to control whether profane words are masked in live transcription and saved meeting transcripts.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; rationales
claims.claim: Filtering is on by default and preserves existing transcript-masking behaviour.
claims.quote: The setting will be on by default, preserving the current transcript-masking behavior unless an administrator changes the assigned policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Turning filtering off allows previously masked words to appear unmasked in live transcription.
claims.quote: When the setting is off, words that would otherwise be masked can appear in live transcription and in the saved transcript.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Turning filtering off allows previously masked words to appear unmasked in the saved transcript.
claims.quote: When the setting is off, words that would otherwise be masked can appear in live transcription and in the saved transcript.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The assigned meeting organiser's policy determines filtering for that organiser's scheduled meetings.
claims.quote: If an administrator turns filtering off for the policy assigned to a meeting organizer, words that would otherwise be masked can appear in both the live and saved transcript for that organizer's scheduled meetings.

claims.where: controls[3]; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The feature adds no organiser-level control or organiser/co-organiser per-meeting override.
claims.quote: This change does not add an organizer-level control and does not change each participant's live-caption profanity preference. / Organizers and co-organizers do not receive a per-meeting override.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[2].note; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The transcript setting leaves each participant's live-caption profanity preference unchanged.
claims.quote: Each participant's live-caption profanity preference; live captions continue to use the participant's existing setting.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center path is Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting settings > Recording and transcription > Filter out profane words in live transcription.
claims.quote: A new Filter out profane words in live transcription setting will be available in the applicable Teams meeting policy under Meeting settings > Recording and transcription.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy accepts -Identity and -FilterProfanityInTranscript Enabled or Disabled to manage transcript filtering.
claims.quote:
Controls whether meeting transcripts filter profanity.

Possible values are:

- **Enabled**: Filters profanity from the meeting transcript.
- **Disabled**: Does not filter profanity from the meeting transcript.

claims.claim: The PowerShell reference gives FilterProfanityInTranscript a default of Enabled.
claims.quote:
### -FilterProfanityInTranscript
Controls whether meeting transcripts filter profanity. / | Default value: | Enabled |

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The PowerShell reference still warns that the feature is not fully released and the setting has no effect.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: Transcription can be turned on or off under Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**. / Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. / Toggle **Transcription** **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true or $false controls whether transcription is allowed.
claims.quote: To manage meeting transcription using PowerShell, use the **`-AllowTranscription`** parameter in [Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy] / Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: AllowTranscription controls permission to transcribe rather than the separate profanity-masking setting.
claims.quote: Determines whether post-meeting captions and transcriptions are allowed in a user's meetings. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this to FALSE to prohibit. / -FilterProfanityInTranscript: Controls whether meeting transcripts filter profanity.

claims.claim: Users can update their own live-caption profanity preference in settings.
claims.quote: Users who have already set their preference will keep their current setting. / Users can update this preference in settings at any time.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no administrator UI or API controlling each participant's live-caption profanity preference.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "profanity" "admin" "captions" "filter". Opened meeting-transcription-captions, teams-admin and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; none documents an administrator control for the participant's caption profanity preference.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing for this specific transcript-filtering setting is not yet published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "profanity" "transcripts" "license" Teams. Read roadmap and MC1478003; opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, meeting-transcription-captions and teams-admin. No setting-specific licence stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has published no price or meter for this particular setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams transcript profanity filtering license pricing meter FilterProfanityInTranscript. Read roadmap, MC1478003 and the FilterProfanityInTranscript reference section; opened meeting-transcription-captions and teams-admin. No setting-specific price or meter found.

claims.claim: Teams transcripts are stored with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.
claims.quote: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether downstream Copilot recaps receive masked or unmasked text when this setting is off.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "profanity" "transcript" "Copilot" "masked". Opened copilot-teams-transcription, meeting-transcription-captions, teams-admin and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; none states how this profanity setting affects downstream recap input.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, At rollout; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The cited transcription page documents meeting-policy creation and assignment to specific users or groups.
claims.quote: To specific users: Select your policy, select Manage users > Assign users / To groups: Select the Group policy assignment tab, select Add, enter the group name, select the policy name, and then select Apply.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Global is the default meeting policy for users without an existing policy assignment; custom policies can govern selected users instead.
claims.quote: To apply changes to all users in your organization who don't have an existing policy assignment, use the **Global policy**. To exclude certain users from the global policy, create and assign a custom meeting policy.

claims.claim: No separate tenant-wide master switch for transcript profanity filtering is documented beyond the meeting-policy control.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "profanity" "tenant" "policy". Opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, meeting-transcription-captions and teams-admin; read MC1478003. No separate tenant master switch documented.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; front matter: action; rationales
claims.claim: No administrator action is required to preserve current behaviour.
claims.quote: No action is required to preserve current behavior.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends confirming the business need and reviewing compliance policies and transcript requirements before disabling filtering.
claims.quote: Before turning filtering off, confirm the business need and review whether the change aligns with your organization's compliance policies and transcript requirements.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends notifying compliance, legal and helpdesk teams about previously masked words appearing in saved transcripts.
claims.quote: Notify compliance, legal, and helpdesk teams that saved transcripts may contain profane words that were previously masked.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal transcript guidance if the organisation changes default policy behaviour.
claims.quote: Update internal transcript guidance if your organization changes the default policy behavior.

claims.claim: This is a transcript text-filtering setting, not a feature that takes autonomous actions.
claims.quote: Controls whether meeting transcripts filter profanity. / Enabled: Filters profanity from the meeting transcript. / Disabled: Does not filter profanity from the meeting transcript.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The known implementation burden is administrator and communication time, consistent with a low cost rating while licensing remains unpublished.
claims.quote: Before turning filtering off, confirm the business need and review whether the change aligns with your organization's compliance policies and transcript requirements. / Notify compliance, legal, and helpdesk teams

claims.claim: The cited Learn pages do not document the admin-center location of the new profanity-filter setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Filter out profane words in live transcription". Opened meeting-transcription-captions, teams-admin and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. The first lacks the setting, the release note describes behaviour without a path, and the reference documents PowerShell.

claims.claim: The cited role reference describes meeting-policy permissions generally rather than naming a role specifically for this profanity-filter setting.
claims.quote: Searched the opened using-admin-roles page for the feature-specific permission: it lists management of meeting policies generally and contains no profanity-filter-specific role. Also read the FilterProfanityInTranscript section of Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, which names no role.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The controls table includes the meeting-policy assignment control that the governance checklist tells administrators to inventory and configure.
claims.quote: List the meeting policies in use ... and identify which organisers each is assigned to. / Assign that policy only to named users or groups ... / The table has filtering, transcription, caption preference and override rows, but no assignment row.
claims.fix: Add a meeting-policy assignment row citing https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-transcription-captions. Give Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Manage users > Assign users for users, and Meetings > Meeting policies > Group policy assignment > Add for groups. The same source documents Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <user> -PolicyName <policy> and -Group <group ID> -PolicyName <policy>.

claims.claim: The controls table represents the separate tenant-wide master switch reported as undocumented in the prose.
claims.quote: Microsoft documents no tenant-wide master switch for it ... / The controls table has no tenant-wide master-switch row.
claims.fix: Add a row governing a separate tenant-wide transcript profanity-filter master switch, with scope tenant and both ui and api null. Explain that no separate master switch is documented and that the Global meeting policy is the default for users without another assignment.
